\begin{document}
Near the first resonance we use the reduced detuning
\begin{equation}
x = \frac{\omega-\epsilon_1}{\Gamma_1}
\label{eq:x1}
\end{equation}
and the transmission is a Lorentzian,
\begin{equation}
T(\omega) = \frac{1}{1+x^2} .
\label{eq:t1}
\end{equation}
Near the second resonance, with
\begin{equation}
x = \frac{\omega-\epsilon_2}{\Gamma_2} ,
\label{eq:x2}
\end{equation}
it has the same shape,
\begin{equation}
T(\omega) = \frac{1}{x^2+1} .
\label{eq:t2}
\end{equation}
\end{document}
